newsitem.title: THAILAND: German, Thai firms to build power plant.
newsitem.headline: German, Thai firms to build power plant.

text.p: A German power company said on Wednesday it signed a joint venture agreement with Thai-Lao Power Co Ltd to invest on the construction of a power plant in Laos.
Energie-Versorgung Schwaben AG signed the agreement with Thai-Lao Power to construct a 700-megawatt lignite-fired power plant near the Laotian town of Hongsa, a statement said..
Operation of the plant is due to start in 2001 and electricity would be supplied from it to Thailand, it said.

Investment cost of the plant is about $1 billion. Thai-Lao Power capital for the venture is set at $300 million of which the German firm holds 20 percent. Project financing for the remaining $700 million will be funded by various import and export banks of suppliers and foreign and local financial institutions the statement said.
Thai-Lao Power is a subsidiary of Thai-Lao Lignite Co Ltd, a Thai investment group which is engaged in several industries in Thailand.
